extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, and educated public interested in science, agriculture, education, and policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries and reportage of recent developments, institutional proposals, standards, and recommendations across scientific, agricultural, educational, and technical domains as presented in a Nature news/notes issue. Focus is on communicating findings, recommended practices, and policy suggestions to the scientific community and interested public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forestry improvement inquiry items
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquire into and report upon the following matters relating to the improvement of forestry in Ireland, viz.: — (i) the present provision for State aid to forestry in Ireland; (a) the means whereby in connection with the operation of the Land Purchase Acts existing woods may be preserved, and land suitable for forestry acquired for public purposes; and (3) the financial and other provisions necessary for a comprehensive scheme of afforestation in Ireland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of the milling research institute
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed objects: to carry out practical research and scientific investigation on grain during storing, milling, working up and baking; to experiment with the baking of home and imported grain; to conduct research work for the Government; and to carry out official and private analyses of grain, flour, fodder stuffs, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute should provide administrative offices and laboratories, experimental granary, mills and bakery, and be fitted with modern machinery to ensure a proper and complete investigation of problems of the milling and baking industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheep parasite treatment regimen
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend dipping twice at an interval of ten days to clear the sheep of these pests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: eggs of parasites (e.g. red lice and sheep Acarus) hatch some days after dipping and are not affected by a single dip; a second dip about ten days later prevents re-establishment and preserves the value of 'dipping orders'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic representation in biological illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological plates and figures should give a natural representation of specimens (e.g. larval feeding and behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid photographic reproductions from museum preparations that do not show natural posture or behavior; strive for plates that are of both scientific and practical value by depicting natural conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-supported applied research as model
rubrics_metrics.description: Model of state-supported research institutes (example: German milling research institute built with a grant from the Minister of Agriculture and maintained jointly by industry bodies) as a means to ensure thorough practical and scientific investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast drawn with reliance on private enterprise; suggests state grants and joint maintenance can ensure comprehensive investigation and support of national industry needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-temperature coefficient measurement method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a modification of Fizeau's method where interference occurs between rays reflected at the top surface of a sheet of black glass (supporting a hollow cylinder of material) and those reflected from the under surface of a sheet of clear glass; place apparatus in an exhausted chamber so temperature corrections are obviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This arrangement permits accurate measurement of coefficients of expansion of solids at low temperatures by avoiding temperature-correction complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for adopting insulated aluminium conductors
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider jointing quality (mechanical and 'sweated' joints claimed superior to wire), conductivity relative to copper (about 60%), required increase in diameter for same current (approx. 28%), claimed weight savings (about 50%), and insulation material (vulcanised bitumen recommended as lighter than paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field experiments and trials are necessary to test commercial utility and cost implications; jointing difficulties historically prevented use but are claimed overcome by makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation features for new wireless telephony systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess systems by their method of generating oscillations (e.g. spark gap with rotating arrangement producing many sparks per second), the microphone design (e.g. hydraulic/capillary microphone producing variations in fluid contact/current), and the choice of transmitting source (comparison of spark-gap results with Poulsen arc in nitrogen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity and strength of telephonic currents in experiments, and consider practical advantages of different transmitters and microphone designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological reporting standards and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily and weekly weather reports should be improved by expanding map observations (e.g. include observations from Iceland and the Azores) and by incorporating wireless telegraphy statistical observations from commanders of ships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced geographic coverage and incorporation of shipborne wireless observations improve the usefulness and accuracy of meteorological maps and statistical reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and safety considerations for standard time distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe apparatus and method employed for time-control by discussing each operation separately and illustrating components with diagrams; identify causes of accidents and the special artifices adopted for eliminating their possibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough, operation-by-operation exposition and diagrammatic illustration are recommended; emphasize accident causes and mitigation measures in system design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic measurement of schoolchildren for physical data
rubrics_metrics.description: "In view of the national importance of obtaining data on the question of physical deterioration, this association urges upon the Government the pressing necessity of instituting, in connection with the medical inspection of school children, a system of periodic measurement which will provide definite information on their physical condition and development."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurements should be instituted in connection with medical inspection so that definite longitudinal data on physical condition and development are available for policy and health assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central supervision and uniform basis for school measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Central authority (preferably a medical bureau or Board of Education with cooperation of medical staffs) should give supervision so that observations may be made on a uniform basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform measurement protocols and central supervision are desirable to ensure comparability; speakers noted large perturbations and inaccuracies and the need to state standards of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical method for tracking individual growth types
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot age as the abscissa and height, weight or girth as the ordinate; draw a series of nearly equidistant curves to show progressive development of multiple grades so an individual can be compared both with the average and with his own type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diagrams that allow plotting of an individual boy's course and comparison with twenty different grades to see relative changes among height, weight, and girth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum appropriateness as pupils mature
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust curriculum as pupils mature: 'With older and cleverer pupils pure nature-study methods become insufficient... the theory of evolution was beyond the grasp of any but the best class.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide more solid, systematic material for older pupils; descriptive and systematic work (e.g. in botany) is advocated to remedy defects in observation and description from early nature-study methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific/girls' education from a domestic point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme of scientific education for girls might radiate from the household: instead of chalk and salt, the common materials of the household (flour, starch, coal, meat, sugar, etc.) should be used as starting points for a girl's study of science; the science of bread-making would lead to cooperation of all helpful studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize domestic-relevant science to make scientific education for girls practical and integrated with household contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites and teacher qualifications for trade classes
rubrics_metrics.description: No student should take a trade class until he has laid a foundation of pure science; good results are obtained when a science teacher is paired with a competent artisan demonstrator; teachers should keep abreast of trade by being known to local factory owners and encouraged to visit factories; the teacher of trades must have had trade experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine sound scientific foundation with practical demonstrators and ensure teacher trade experience; cooperation of parents, teachers, employers, and trade-union leaders is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade school schedule and maintenance provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure courses so that 'six half-days are devoted to trade teaching, four half-days to general instruction'; pupils in day trade schools mostly hold scholarships with maintenance grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course planning should balance trade instruction and general education and provide maintenance support for pupils (scholarships/grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against mistaken specialisation by monitoring labour market
rubrics_metrics.description: The labour market must be watched to guard against mistaken specialisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design specialised training with awareness of labour demand to avoid training for obsolete or oversupplied skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific photographic survey recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain information as to the present state of things in Britain in connection with photo-survey work; publish instructions, or give advice, for the execution of a scientific photographic survey; and endeavour to found or promote a photo-record of the town and district in which the British Association holds its annual meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide published instructions/advice for scientific photo-survey execution and encourage local photo-record projects associated with annual meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local societies should correlate local specialist facts on natural areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provincial scientific society should seek to correlate, from a geographical point of view, all the facts obtained by specialists in its own locality, taking as a basis a natural area rather than a county boundary; work should be systematic and on uniform principles throughout the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlation by a person of special training can yield deductions valuable to future specialists; systematic uniform principles are needed before a complete geographical conception of the land is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify achievable standards of accuracy for school measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern expressed that perturbations and inaccuracies in obtaining measurements of growth are considerable, so that final results may be nearly valueless; speakers noted that no one indicated exactly what standards of accuracy were possible or desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When instituting measurement programs, explicitly state the standards of accuracy achievable and desirable to ensure data usefulness; consider measurement precision and sampling practices.
